Where the work is done

items.text: For tax years beginning after 31 December 2024, under Section 174A. Spreading it over 60 months or more is optional.

pieces.post: Friday 27 November: founder shares and the 30 day 83(b) election
pieces.format_hook: deadline explainer, opens with who it affects and the 30 days
text: If you received founder shares that vest, one tax form has a 30 day deadline, and it starts the day the shares are issued to you.
It is the 83(b) election. The IRS's own form for it, Form 15620, says it must be filed no later than 30 days after the date the property was transferred.

Here is what it changes. Without the election, shares that vest over time count as income for your services when they vest: their value at that point, minus what you paid. With it, you count that difference now, at the value when the shares were issued.
A worked example: if you paid the full fair market value of your shares when they were issued, the difference is zero, so the election reports no income now.

How it is filed: sign Form 15620, mail it to the IRS office where you file your federal income tax return, and give a copy to your company. For shares transferred since 1 January 2016, you no longer attach a copy to your tax return.

What to do this week: find the date your shares were issued and count 30 days. If you are inside the window, decide with your accountant or attorney before it closes. The election is not required, and whether it suits you depends on what you paid and what the shares are worth. Keep proof of the date you mailed it.
Did you file an 83(b) when you received your founder shares?

pieces.post: Saturday 28 November: contractor paperwork, red flag or green flag
pieces.format_hook: lighter post, red flag or green flag, opens with the format's label and the 31 December check
text: Red flag or green flag: three things in your contractor files to check before 31 December.
One. A US contractor you paid this year has never sent you a Form W-9.

Red flag. The W-9 is how a US payee gives you their correct taxpayer identification number for the information returns you file, such as their Form 1099-NEC. And when a payee has not given you that number in the required manner, the IRS says the payer must withhold a flat 24% from payments such as contractor fees.
Two. Your contractor abroad sent you a signed Form W-8BEN.

Green flag. When you hold a valid Form W-8 that you can reliably match to the payment, the IRS's instructions for requesters say you are exempt from reporting it on a Form 1099 and from backup withholding.
Three. That W-8BEN was signed in 2023.

Red flag from 1 January. A Form W-8 is generally valid from the date signed until the last day of the third calendar year after that, unless a change in circumstances makes it incorrect. So a form signed in 2023 generally runs out on 31 December 2026.
What to do this month: list every contractor you paid in 2026, note which form you hold for each and the date it was signed, then request the missing W-9s and any W-8 that runs out this year.
Which form takes longer to collect on your team, the W-9 or the W-8BEN?

pieces.post: Sunday 29 November: six dates from 15 December to 15 April
pieces.format_hook: reference calendar, opens with the six dates and the span
text: Six dates to put in your company calendar now, from 15 December to 15 April.

Tuesday 15 December 2026. A calendar year corporation that pays estimated tax makes its last 2026 installment. Installments are due on the 15th day of the 4th, 6th, 9th and 12th months of the tax year.
Friday 15 January 2027. The last 2026 estimated tax payment for individuals. You can skip it if you file your 2026 return by 1 February 2027 and pay the entire balance with it.
Monday 1 February 2027. Forms 1099-NEC go to each contractor and to the IRS. The rule says 31 January, which is a Sunday in 2027, so the next business day applies.
Monday 1 March 2027. A Delaware corporation's annual report and franchise tax. Missing it brings a $200 penalty, and interest of 1.5% a month on unpaid tax.
Monday 15 March 2027. Form 1065 for calendar year partnerships, and Form 1120-S for calendar year S corporations.
Thursday 15 April 2027. Form 1120 for calendar year C corporations.
Not every date applies to every company. What to do this week: mark the ones that apply to yours in a shared calendar, set a reminder two weeks before each, and name who owns it.
Which of these six is already on your company's calendar?
